newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end higher, outlook still grim.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end higher, outlook still grim.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended higher on a technically driven rebound on Wednesday as players moved to cover their short positions after the market broke above a key level in late trade.
Dealers said there was no fresh news behind the rise and it was unlikely to be sustained in the near term as the lead September Nikkei 225 contract continued to face resistance on the higher end.
"When it neared 19,800, I decided to sell it because I don't think it'll go up to 20,000," said a senior trader at a Japanese futures house.
The September Nikkei added 265 points to close at 19,715 after falling to a low of 19,230 in early trade. Volume was a moderate 18,900 lots.
"It looks like the market is just trading on technicals. There was some short-covering after it broke 19,500," the trader said.
Taiwan stock index futures ended slightly lower as Taipei shares weakened amid soaring money market rates and expectations of impending rate hikes by commercial banks.
The August MSCI contract shed 0.9 point to end at 413.4 on volume of 1,815 lots.
